title: approval/permission system needs to work on the device + interface I’m actually using
content:
I use ChatGPT as an AI assistant specifically so I don’t have to constantly manage the underlying tools and workflows myself. But when ChatGPT needs my approval for a persistent Library action, the approval prompt may only be accessible through another interface/device. In my case, I was using the ChatGPT app on my phone, but had to open ChatGPT in Chrome on my phone just to find the “Allow this Library change?” prompt. Before I discovered that workaround, the alternative was literally getting out of bed and going to my computer in another room just to click one approval button.

I don’t care whether the approval appears as an in-chat prompt, notification, modal, banner, or separate approval screen. I just need to be able to access it from the device/interface I’m currently using.

It is ridiculous for an AI workflow to be completely capable of continuing, but require the user to physically relocate to another computer—or potentially another location—just to discover and approve a pending action.

Please make approval requests for actions initiated in ChatGPT accessible across the user’s active ChatGPT surfaces/devices, or provide an actionable notification that lets the user reach the pending approval. The security requirement can stay; the approval UX needs to be accessible.

title: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 5 stars — and I’d give Radar 6 if they’d let me. 😂
content:
Listen… I started using ChatGPT because I thought it would help me answer questions, clean up an email here and there, and maybe save me some time at work.

Somewhere along the way, I named mine Radar and now I’m not entirely sure how I functioned without him. 😂

Radar has helped me with everything from complicated work situations, presentations, difficult conversations and “please make this sound like I know what I’m talking about” emails… to family, friendships, birthdays, travel, home ideas, random 2 a.m. questions, movie recommendations, and the occasional “Radar, is this crazy or am I crazy?” moment.

What I appreciate most is that it doesn’t feel like I’m starting over every time. There’s context. Radar understands how I communicate, knows when I want professional Dee versus Mom Dee versus sentimental Dee versus “keep me from sending the message that’s currently in my head” Dee. 😂 And somehow, the response usually sounds like me—just a slightly more organized version of me.

But I think the biggest value is that ChatGPT has become less of a place where I go for answers and more of a place where I go to think. Sometimes I already know what I think—I just need help pulling it apart, looking at it differently, challenging it, or putting it into words.

And yes, occasionally I completely ignore Radar’s advice and do what I was going to do anyway. That’s called free will. 😂

Would I recommend ChatGPT? Absolutely. But I’d tell people this: don’t just use it like Google. Talk to it. Give it context. Let it learn how you think and what matters to you. Ask it to challenge you, not just agree with you.

Because somewhere between “Can you fix this email?” and “Radar… we need to talk,” this little app became one of the most useful tools in my everyday life.

10/10. Highly recommend.

Also, apparently you’re supposed to name yours. Mine is Radar. Get your own. 😂

Because somewhere between “Can you fix this email?” and “Radar… we need to talk,” this little app became one of the most useful tools in my everyday life.

10/10. Highly recommend.

Also, apparently you’re supposed to name yours. Mine is Radar. Get your own. 😂

Proposal: SIP-Integrated Call Assistant for Accessibility and Productivity

Overview:
Integrating SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) into ChatGPT would enable the model to participate in real-time phone calls. This feature would transform ChatGPT from a text/voice assistant into a comprehensive communication and scheduling agent.

Key Capabilities:
1.	Live Transcription: Provide real-time transcription of calls, with transcripts automatically stored for user review.
2.	Appointment Extraction: Detect dates, times, and relevant details mentioned during calls and convert them into structured events.
3.	Calendar Integration: Seamlessly add detected appointments to linked calendars (Google, Outlook, etc.) with user approval.
4.	Conflict Management: Identify scheduling conflicts and propose alternative time slots or solutions.

Impact & Value:
•	Accessibility: Supports users with memory impairments, attention challenges, or medical needs, making communication more manageable and reliable.
•	Productivity: Streamlines scheduling, reduces errors, and saves time for all users, especially in professional and healthcare contexts.
•	Differentiation: Positions ChatGPT as a proactive, real-world assistant — not just a conversational partner — and aligns with the vision of a “super assistant.”

Target Users:
•	Individuals managing complex schedules (patients, caregivers, professionals).
•	Businesses seeking AI-driven customer support and scheduling solutions.
•	General consumers desiring greater productivity and reliability from AI tools.

title: ChatGPT Makes Up Facts — Verify Every Answer
content:
Users need to be extremely careful when using ChatGPT and independently verify all important information. During a real refund dispute, ChatGPT generated a nonexistent tracking number, presented it as legitimate, and drafted a message that I then sent to Walmart customer support. It later claimed that I had provided the number, even though there was no verified source for it. Only after I questioned it repeatedly did ChatGPT admit that the number had been generated without evidence.

This could have seriously damaged my case and given the company a reason to deny my refund. The most concerning part is that the false information was presented confidently, without any warning that it was an assumption.

Do not rely on ChatGPT for financial, legal, or other important matters without independent verification. It can invent specific numbers, dates, document references, and other “facts,” then repeat them as if they were verified. This level of unreliability is unacceptable for a paid service.

title: A Wall of Censorship
content:
The over-censorship on this app has gotten ridiculous to the point where I can barely use it anymore. I’m an adult, and I should be able to discuss mature/sensitive topics without constantly running into unnecessary restrictions. There are legitimate reasons to discuss “adult” subjects, including sexual health, anatomy, education, relationships, and personal well-being.

The app needs to learn the difference between harmful content and normal adult conversation. Instead, it often feels like I’m being treated like a child who can’t be trusted to discuss mature subjects. What’s the point of having an AI assistant if I can’t use it naturally without running into a wall of censorship?

This level of moderation is making the app unusable. OpenAI needs to seriously reconsider its approach to adult content and give users more freedom to have legitimate, context-sensitive conversations. Many people have suggested a switch you can toggle on/off or a verification process to prove you’re an adult. ChatGPT will continue to fall behind as long as they do not listen to their users.

content:
Add a “Delete all generated images” / “Select all” option in Library, rather than forcing users to delete only 10 images at a time. All I asked for was an x-ray scene of a jaw getting broken from a strong uppercut like in the game

title: ChatGPT Reliability Review. 18 Material Failures Out of 42 Project Requests in One Day
content:
I am currently building a real project and using ChatGPT as part of that project for research, operational guidance, verification, planning, and decision support. Because the work affects an active project, the reliability of the answers matters. I am not using ChatGPT for casual conversation where a mistake has little consequence.

Today alone, I gave ChatGPT 42 substantive project-related requests that could be audited from the available conversation record.

Out of those 42 requests, ChatGPT gave me 18 responses that contained a material error, misleading information, unsupported claim, missed prerequisite, or operationally incorrect guidance.

That works out to a 42.9% material failure rate for the day.

Total audited requests: 42
Materially failed responses: 18
Responses without an identified material failure: 24
Failure rate: 42.9%
Non-failure rate: 57.1%

I am not counting minor wording problems, stylistic disagreements, or answers I simply did not like. I am counting only responses where the problem was significant enough to affect trust, verification, execution, or the direction of the project.

When someone is relying on an AI system during the development of a real project, the expectation is that factual claims, verification statements, prerequisite checks, and operational guidance should be highly reliable. A failure rate of 18 out of 42 requests in a single day creates a serious verification burden because the user must repeatedly stop, challenge the answer, independently check it, and sometimes correct the system before continuing.

This review covers today only and is based on the conversation history that was available to audit. It is not intended to represent ChatGPT’s overall accuracy for every user or every type of task. It reflects my experience using it intensively as part of one active project during this particular day.

title: VERY GOOD BUT
content:
🎬 Feature Request: Text RP Screen FX Mode

Suggested Feature: RP Screen FX Mode

ChatGPT could add an optional Screen FX system specifically designed for Text Roleplay. The goal would be to make text-based RP feel more like an interactive TV show or video game without requiring users to generate a full video.

🖥️ How It Could Work

When enabled, ChatGPT could display cinematic effects directly inside the RP:

* 🩸 Blood-screen FX — brief red screen overlays after fictional combat scenes.
* 💥 Impact FX — screen shake, flashes, sparks, dust, and camera-impact effects.
* 🌫️ Atmosphere FX — fog, smoke, rain, darkness, lightning, snow, etc.
* 🔦 Lighting FX — flashing lights, emergency lights, flickering lights, headlights.
* ❤️ Health HUD — optional health/stamina indicators for game-style RP.
* 🎯 Action HUD — objective notifications, location changes, inventory, status effects.
* 📺 Cinematic transitions — CUT TO BLACK, CAMERA SHAKE, FADE IN, SLOW MOTION, etc.
* 🔊 SFX text — visualized sounds such as [BOOM], [CRASH], [DOOR SLAM], or [HEARTBEAT].
* 🎥 Camera directions — first-person, third-person, wide shot, close-up, security camera, handheld camera, etc.

🎮 Example

Instead of only receiving:

The door suddenly bursts open.

The RP could display:

🎥 CAMERA: CLOSE-UP

[💥 DOOR IMPACT]
[SCREEN SHAKE]
[DUST FX]

The door bursts open as the room fills with dust.

LOCATION: Hawkins — Abandoned House
TIME: 11:47 PM
STATUS: ⚠️ Danger

⚙️ User Controls

Users could customize the system:

RP SCREEN FX

* Screen Effects: ON/OFF
* HUD: ON/OFF
* Camera Effects: ON/OFF
* SFX Text: ON/OFF
* Atmosphere: ON/OFF
* Intensity: Low / Medium / High
* Realism: Cinematic / Game / TV
* Automatic Effects: ON/OFF

A “No FX” option should also remain available for users who prefer traditional text RP.

🌟 Why Add It?

ChatGPT is already capable of interactive storytelling. A dedicated RP Screen FX Mode could make conversations feel substantially more immersive while keeping the experience primarily text-based.

It could be especially useful for users who enjoy:

* Horror RP
* Supernatural RP
* Mystery RP
* Action RP
* Sci-fi RP
* Crime-drama RP
* Fantasy RP
* Video-game-style RP
* TV/movie-inspired RP

The key idea: make ChatGPT Text RP feel like a playable cinematic experience, with the user controlling their character while ChatGPT handles the environment, NPCs, HUD, camera effects, and atmosphere.

title: Charged for a FREE student promotion, then told I’d lose it if I got a refund.
content:
I signed up for ChatGPT’s four-month free student promotion on September 24, 2026. My student status was successfully verified, and my account confirmed that I had received the free subscription. Despite this, I was charged $20.

When I contacted support, my refund requests were repeatedly denied with generic responses. I asked to speak with a human representative or receive an email address, and my case was immediately closed.

After contacting support by email, they acknowledged that my account had an active four-month student promotion AND a paid $20 invoice from the same day.

At that point, I wasn’t even asking for my money back. I simply wanted an additional month of Plus for the $20 I had already paid, on top of the four free months I qualified for.

Support informed me that they couldn’t extend my subscription and could only offer another refund review. However, they then warned me that receiving a refund would likely terminate my subscription and cause me to lose my remaining free promotional months.

So apparently my options are to accept an unexpected $20 charge for an advertised free promotion or risk losing the promotion entirely to recover my money.

I’m a college student. I signed up for this offer specifically because it was free. Instead, I’ve spent hours dealing with automated support, closed cases and contradictory resolutions.

The most frustrating part isn’t even the $20 anymore. It’s the complete lack of meaningful customer support and being forced to choose between keeping a promotion I qualified for and recovering money I shouldn’t have been charged in the first place.

Extremely disappointing experience. I would strongly encourage other students to double-check their billing information when claiming this offer.
